fiji.rule: One property (canon, 1.6A): the lattice follows the applied field inside its 550-1400 K window. Moving it changes where it sits in the field, not what it can do. In the shield shadow (FG-5) it adds 0.3 % of the stop field for ~700 t per engine; the existing liner adds nothing measurable. A visible field-shaping role needs the coercive orientation (SP-17C).
fiji.display: lattice_activation stays a thermal-state and readiness indicator (activation glow from 650 K); no animation shows the lattice bending the field.

concepts.note: Masses per engine. A+ adds no joint and no tread; its service petals are shells, not field hardware, so they add hinge mass only where a service opening is wanted (counted as zero here; a design choice for Phase F).

scores.basis: judgement from the concept rows: joints, treads and petals cost credibility, mass and maintenance; A+ adds service petals that open only cold, which helps maintenance and startup visuals without touching the field

states.description: Rings stowed and locked forward, rotors still, coils at zero, petals shut.
Locks release; L4 runs aft on the rails to its operating station; service lines pay out; locks engage; dynamo rotors spin up.
Metrology scans the loops; carriages trim position and tilt from the as-stowed error to the fine tolerance; the AI checks clearances, locks and the predicted field.
Dynamos pump the coils to the stop field (31-307 h at 1-0.1 V), persistent switches close, rotors stop; the lattice is heated through activation to its operating point.
Low-power test pulses; trim coils adjust the topology; the AI compares the predicted and measured plume and converges.
The bootstrap flywheel feeds the first driver pulses; the burn starts; exhaust appears.
All locks and the alignment in tolerance, calibration residual below the threshold: lock indicators close round each engine, then across the four.
Pulse rate and flux shares follow the throttle; trim coils steer; only the plume, the diagnostics and the four-engine balance change.
Pulses stop; coils stay persistent or ramp down by the dynamos run backwards; after cool-down the rings stow. A fault ends in its own trip.

sequence.display_time: The viewer compresses time per state and shows the physical duration beside it; nothing pretends field formation takes seconds.

method: rigid transforms only (no deformation, no skinning, no morph targets)
one shared mesh per moving part type, one node per engine (the effect-object pattern), so download grows by nodes, not meshes
a per-state pose table (JSON) interpolated in JS in the viewer, as effect_states already is for opacities; no glTF animation channels
field lines: precomputed polylines per state drawn as one line batch; plasma flow: a dash-offset shader along the same lines
diagnostic overlays (control, energy, thermal, sync) as HTML/canvas panels, not 3D geometry
view modes switch layers on and off; the default exterior view shows hardware and plume only
tread tiles (if ever used) instanced; dynamo rotors instanced
browser.caution: Draw calls today: 5,241 in the default exterior view (Vertex 1.2 evidence). Every number here is an estimate; frame time is measured in Phase F on the viewer (evidence class SW in the cloud, HW on a real GPU) before anything ships.

steps.what: Owner decisions: concept, SP-18A status, Phase F go
Pure geometry: carriage stations (stowed, canon) and service-petal hinge axes as parameters; motion limits as functions
Split the moving groups out of the merged families: the L4 ring (coil, cryostat, structure, armour, hot), the L1/L2 cryostat shells
Per-engine moving objects in the cluster sharing one mesh each, parented at the engine placement (the effect-object pattern); the static engine instance keeps everything else
Controller: the proposed properties on DRIVE_MANIFOLD_CTRL, per-engine where needed; drivers for location/rotation; nine STATES
Root machinery parts: dynamo housings and rotors at the six lead turrets, persistent-switch boxes, flywheel at the hub
Review file WORK_VTX18 with the nine states as markers and cameras (Phase F)
Inspection: clearance and motion-limit checks for every pose (ring overlap, lock positions, envelope)
Export: per-state pose table and field-line polylines next to the GLB; web viewer interpolation and view modes
Measure: draw calls, frame time, download before and after on the same views (GFX method)

reused: all four loops, windings, cryostat segments and joint flanges
modified: VTX_MAGNETIC_NOZZLE_* and VTX_SHIELDING_armour, VTX_STRUCTURE_structure, VTX_HOT_THERMAL_hot families (split by moving group)
lead and cryogen branches, lithium jumpers of L4 (flexible festoon form)
new: HTS dynamo housings and rotors (6 per engine)
carriage drive and lock blocks (8 per ring)

verdict.statement: Recommend A+: rings that telescope on the existing longerons and align to sub-millimetre, leadless dynamos that spin only while the field forms, a shared ignition flywheel, trim coils for the fast layer, service petals that open only cold, and engineering view modes for field, plasma, energy, heat, control and synchronization. Field petals are not recommended: a petal that moves a winding cuts it, and at 10 nOhm per joint the inner-loop petals alone would dissipate 26 MW at the radiators and lose persistent current in 61 h. No mechanism here closes capture, source radiation, driver power, coil survival, mass or thermal closure.
